title: contract manifest
$comment: One document per namespace (one deployment of one contract): the contract-level facts and every package's circuit manifest (ARCHITECTURE.md section 7, "The contract manifest"). pss-client's generator (contract-manifest.ts, `pss-manifest build`) writes it from the compiled contract artifact, the compiled circuits and a hand-written descriptor; no slot is copied by hand. Its hash, poseidon2_hash_bytes(JCS(document)), is the manifest hash (testvectors/contract_manifest.json). The document never contains the namespace's own address: a pinned read of the namespace's own contract is written $self. The cross-field rules are the machine's (sidecar-core manifest::contract, run at REGISTER): every package's circuit is an entry of circuits and every entry is used; package names are unique and each circuit manifest's circuit is its package name; an alias names a listed package (one without alias_of) and runs its circuit; at most 32 packages; the listed packages fit contract.package_capacity; under upgrades circuits or contract the package list is at most 14 or 13 (one upgrade's public writes fit one transaction) and queue.stale_blocks is not null; queue, storage and contract.package_capacity are present exactly when a package takes a queued intake, and state_keys, plain_reads and init only then; storage.shared_onchain exactly when a package takes secret-shared on-chain intake; storage.circuit_pins exactly when upgrades is circuits or contract; a queued package names its request keys (state_keys, as many as its circuit manifest takes, each a key of the top-level state_keys), a direct package none; every top-level state key is used and every key read is written by some package; every package on a key gives it one state mode, flat or tree, one tree shape and one flat length, and a tree a round loads is stored back at the key it is loaded from; one intake family per namespace; plain_reads names pinned-read parameters; init names a listed queued package that reads no key and writes at least one.

name.$comment: a label for logs and status pages

node_keys.$comment: whether the contract can change its node key set (the node_keys axis, KeyEpochs or FixedKeys); generated: rotating exactly when the artifact has rotate_keys

upgrades.$comment: what about the deployed app may change; generated: contract when the artifact has upgrade_contract, circuits when it has upgrade_circuits, else fixed

class_id.$comment: the contract class id, from the artifact

package_capacity.$comment: the length of the constructor's Config.tip.packages (a tip contract)

contract.$comment: the contract this document was built for; absent for a namespace without a contract

slot.$comment: the storage slot of the app's Queue

stale_blocks.$comment: the stale period in L2 blocks; null: a head is never skipped

stale_blocks_slot.$comment: the slot of the stored stale period, TipConfig.stale_blocks

circuit_pins.$comment: the slot of the app's CircuitUpgrades (the circuit pins an upgrade schedules, a DelayedPublicMutable, then the upgrade authority); exactly when upgrades is circuits or contract

state_keys.$comment: every state key the rounds touch: its name (the contract's storage field) and commitment slot

plain_reads.$comment: a pinned read's parameter to the slot behind its plain getter, read instead of simulating the call

input_slots.$comment: the slot of each init input in the contract's Config, in order

circuits.$comment: each compiled circuit's vk hash, which REGISTER recomputes from its bytes

alias_of.$comment: another intake of the listed package of this name: the same circuit, verified under that package's pin; the contract's list does not name it

state_keys.$comment: a queued package's request keys by name: $state_keys.reads[i] is reads[i]

manifest.$comment: the circuit manifest (docs/manifest.schema.json; check-manifests.py validates it there)

packages.$comment: the listed packages (those without alias_of) in the contract's list order

name.$comment: 1 to 256 bytes of visible ASCII, as every name a binding hashes
